factMedia.caption: A standard katana, one of the fastest, lightest weapons around.  They rely on skill and dexterity rather than brute strength.  Quality is more important than it is with other types of blade, so they tend to be more expensive.
Traditional heavy duty armour commonly worn by government owned samurai.

The Hivers are extremely proud of the skeleton limbs that they supposedly manufacture themselves.  This arm is obviously made mostly out of salvaged parts from other skeleton arms, though they did make a functioning claw hand for it, quite an impressive feat of engineering in this age.  The limb cap is half a grog can with some padding inside.
They are good and cheap, but not very durable, and obviously your dexterity is going to suffer from having a claw for a hand.
A basic first aid kit made up of various bandages, used to stop people from bleeding to death.  The poor quality will limit you if it is lower than your skills, resulting in slower healing.
A cheap and lightweight weapon from the swamps.  It's not very powerful, but it can be used to spray an opponent with bolts at close range before switching to a sword.

A small and light backpack that will help you carry extra supplies, and can be ditched in an emergency.  The comfortable weight distribution allows you to carry a lot more weight, and will only slow you down very slightly in a fight.

An extremely old set of samurai armour that is rusting away to nothing.
These shackles are faulty and don't do a very good job of hindering prisoners.
The religious book of the Holy Nation, every citizen has to have one by law.

Gifted to Shager's most loyal Invincible Warrior, Ida the Flying Bull.

For him, I fight a thousand men. For him, I die a thousand deaths.
A sword-cleaver hybrid, it's lighter and more suited to normal combat.
An unusual weapon design that supposedly came from the deserts.  Usually hard to find, but they have a distinct ability to gut spiders really well, making them popular with certain specialists.

A hefty sword once taken from a defeated Shek Guardian. 

Without their name, their status, or their prized weapons, the shamed ones walk the land forever as lost ghosts.

A ridiculously unwieldy weapon sometimes used by Skeletons.  Requiring both dexterity and strength to use properly, they are widely known as "Suicide Blades", because they often get their users killed.
A nasty weapon, designed for hacking through meat.  The crude bluntness of the weapon means victims don't bleed to death so often, they just get hacked and maimed.

A pretty exotic weapon, thought to have originated from the Black Desert.  Not very popular for some reason and people will probably laugh at you in bars, but is actually a defensive masterpiece and shouldn't be underestimated.
A huge axe built to work like a sword.  Stupidly heavy, but it impresses the ladies.  Shek ladies mostly.

An uncommon katana modification sacrificing defence by removing the guard.  It's more a psychological advantage than a physical one, knowing subconsciously that attack is your best defence promotes a more aggressive combat style.  Gang bosses and Jonin tend to use them to equip their underlings because it makes trouble-makers on both sides more reluctant.
A professional law-enforcement weapon.  Designed for non-lethal takedowns, it has a sword-catcher guard that gives an advantage when defending.
An unusual sabre-polearm hybrid that mitigates the disadvantages of using a polearm.
A portion of metal cut out of the far end of the blade makes it slightly faster and more manoeuvrable.  Most swordsmen can't notice the difference, others swear by it.

The classic sabre.  Does more damage than a regular katana, at the cost of extra weight.  The heavier blade is better for defending, but still curved for cutting damage.  They're very common, so can usually be found cheaper than other weapons of similar quality.
A basic iron stick with a wrapped handle.

headings: Homemade (Does not exist, if they did however these would be their stats)

factMedia.caption: An iron stick, used to hit things.

A professional law-enforcement weapon.  Designed for non-lethal takedowns, it has a sword-catcher guard that gives an advantage when defending.  The smaller 1-handed version makes a good sidearm and has an advantage in tight indoor situations.
Close to being classed as a heavy weapon, it's the heaviest cleaver you will find.
Very light for a sabre, but too straight and heavy to classify as a katana.  They are popular among nobles as a status symbol in the empire.
A hefty club used by wealthier bandit types.

Most blades, like katanas and sabres, use their curvature to "slide" off the target, increasing the amount of cut damage. The reverse curvature of a Moon Cleaver does the opposite, catching limbs and necks, keeping the force of the blow driving inwards.
A katana-polearm hybrid that mitigates the disadvantages of using a naginata, but still too long to be comfortable indoors.
A samurai hunter's weapon that can be deceptively fast and hard to defend against.  Too long to use effectively in cramped environments, but good against animals.
A smaller, lighter katana with a straight blade that is easier to produce.  Popular with ninjas because they're better for stabbing people in the back with, but not the best for toe-to-toe combat.
An extended katana variant with increased reach and damage.
The Cross is the revered holy weapon and symbol of the Paladins.  With it they have been slaying skeletons and people they think might be skeletons for centuries.

A hefty hacking weapon, with a good reach.  A nice balance for those who find fragment axes too clumsy and blunt, the plank retains some of the extra deadly traits of a regular sword, while still remaining ridiculously crude.

Unusual weapons that are sometimes used by hunters as their reach makes them good for taking down animals.  Due to their cumbersome length however they are at a serious disadvantage when used indoors.

A classic hard-hitting blade used by many legendary swordsmen, including Arc himself.  The rings are pretty noisy and mainly designed to distract and annoy the hell out of your opponent.  Beak Things hate it, but it tends to just make them more vicious.
A lightweight version of the combat cleaver that can be worn on the hip.
A nasty weapon that causes bleeding in addition to crushing damage.
Popular with poor farmers, pacifists and drifters.  It's usually seen as a weapon for those who can't afford a blade, but sometimes can make a fool of a good swordsman.

A hybrid between katana and sabre, it has a top-heavy balance that feels odd to a katana user, hence the name.  It's fast and has a similar reach to a Nodachi.

A mostly forgotten weapon in modern times, it was once popular among mercenaries of the old empire.
Smaller and lighter, usually used as a sidearm for backup.  It's worth noting that although short, it has a major advantage when fighting indoors against longer weapons.
Heavies pack a serious punch but don't have much range due to their weight.
High accuracy, long-range bolts.  You won't go wrong with these.
Despite the name, Regulars vary a fair bit in size and weight, but they all sort of fall into a range that works in most bows.  They've become a common standard and are easy to find anywhere.
Toothpicks are the smallest bolts available.  They don't pack a lot of punch but are usually used in rapid fire weapons.

A rare, extreme long-range weapon for snipers.  It's possible to do a lot of damage with one of these before an enemy even realises what is happening to them.  Takes skill to use effectively, and not much use at short range.
A poor quality attempt at crafting a Toothpick.  A pretty worthless bow.

Based on salvaged old-world blueprints and manufactured by the Tech Hunters.  It's an advanced weapon with a good range and accuracy.  
More expensive and less common than a Ranger, it's usually used by Tech Hunter expeditions venturing into the dangerous "3 Corners" regions of the continent.

A more advanced version than the MkI, it's more complicated to use and unskilled users have a hard time reloading smoothly.  For the experienced archer however it's one of the best long-range weapons available.
A reliable mid-range weapon that's easy to use, especially for amateurs.  It deals out consistent damage at a reasonable rate.  The standard support weapon in mercenary units.

The Spring Bat is a modern invention. Designed by rebels in the formative years of the United Cities, it's easy to build and designed to have the power to punch through the heavy armour of dominating military forces.  It pays for this with short range and poor accuracy.
An extremely old set of samurai armour that is rusting away to nothing.
An extremely old set of samurai armour that is rusting away to nothing.
An extremely old set of samurai armour that is rusting away to nothing.
Heavy armour plates for protecting the neck and face.
An armoured hood, for some kind of heavy-ninja dude.
Salvaged rags, straps and plates pulled together by a decent craftsman has made this monstrosity. Commonly found on wanderers and bandits, it shouldn't be underestimated.

Salvaged rags, straps and plates pulled together by a decent craftsman has made this monstrosity.  This armour has plenty of gaps and vulnerabilities, but allows good freedom of movement for its class.  Commonly found on wanderers and bandits, but is also favoured by duelists.
The strange hat and stormgoggles of the Ashland drifters, strange individuals who have allegedly ventured into the Ashlands and returned, for reasons unknown.
A pair of stormgoggles of the Ashland drifters, strange individuals who have allegedly ventured into the Ashlands and returned, for reasons unknown.

Ragged cloth with plates to protect the sword arm.  It's pretty dire protection, but the wide open mid-section creates an opening that leads to more predictable enemy attacks.  It's lightweight and the arm plates on your forward side allow you to adopt some extra skillful combat tactics.
Keeps sweat and hair out of your eyes.
A hat usually worn by weirdo assassins.  Hides the face and makes you look creepy.
Keeps sweat and hair out of your eyes.
A plated leather jacket with a good solid armour coverage. Commonly worn by the wealthier drifters and professional adventurer scouts.
Black rags typical of down-and-out hobo ninjas

If a Hiver tries wearing a regular human-sized shirt it just sort of hangs loose and falls off their shoulders, often tangling up their arms.  So they were forced to manufacture their own, which they have done to a suspiciously higher standard than all their gear designed for humans.
The best lightweight under-armour that money can buy.  Adds a reliable extra layer of defence to your equipment.
This is basically just wrapping a strip of chainmail around your head, but it does do a good job of protecting you when it's not falling off.
The best lightweight under-armour that money can buy.  Adds a reliable extra layer of defence to your equipment.
Standard Holy Army issue.
A hat with a shade for the eyes, favoured by traders.
Pads your legs, turns a potential slice into a nasty bruise.
Reinforced to pad your legs, turns a potential slice into a nasty bruise.
These actually have hidden chain mail sewn into the lining.  Sneaky.
A chain undershirt provides a reliable second layer of defence.
A chain undershirt provides a reliable second layer of defence.

A medium class leather armour, it's used to equip empire conscripts, partially because they don't usually have the endurance for wearing heavy samurai armour, but mainly because it's cheaper.  Not quite as good as mercenary leather armour.

An exotic suit of heavy armour plates that gives the wearer the toughness and mobility of a big rock.  The Crab Raiders designed this armour with the aim of being more like crabs, with little consideration of other factors.
A very heavy iron hat. As with other eye-slit based helmets, it offers fantastic protection but you can't see a damn thing.
Iron shoes that are pretty painful to wear. The Crab Raiders designed this armour with the aim of being more like crabs, with little consideration of other factors.

An exotic suit of heavy armour plates that gives the wearer the toughness and mobility of a big rock.  The Crab Raiders designed this armour with the aim of being more like crabs, but little consideration of other factors.
Undershirts provide a reliable second layer of defence.
Good solid long-range boots, common amongst travellers.
Lightweight leather leg protection.
A creepy black duster coat worn by wierdos out of the Ashlands.  Provides good protection against the harsh environment.
Dirty rags, worn by slaves and good-for-nothings
Keeps the heat off your head and pads your brains.
Good shirt for sneaking about, doing spy stuff.
Traditional heavy duty armour commonly worn by government owned samurai.
A solid steel helmet, flared at the sides.
A breathing mask that helps mitigate the negative health effects of fog.
Martial artists are a rare oddity in a world of swords and have a reputation as eccentrics.  They are however the bane of slavers, because they can never be disarmed.

Head plates were invented by an old forgotten clan that was obsessed with luck.  Before battle they used prophets and shamans to predict where on their head the next fatal blow was due to land, then position the metal plate on their head accordingly.  Sometimes it worked, sometimes it didn't.  Such is luck, they would say.
A metal cage-armoured jacket.
Metal cage-armoured pants.

These actually have hidden chain mail sewn into the lining.  Sneaky.

This armour is nice and light without hampering mobility, it will protect your heart and that's it. It's designed to be worn over chain or leather armour as an extra layer of protection, although most people don't for some reason.  Probably because they can't afford any.
Heavy prisoner shackles. They stop you from running and doing a lot of things. They also trip you up in combat. They are locked on, you need to pick the lock somehow.

If a Hiver tries wearing a regular human-sized shirt it just sort of hangs loose and falls off their shoulders, often tangling up their arms.  So they were forced to manufacture their own, which they have done to a suspiciously higher standard than all their gear designed for humans.
It gives near perfect protection of the body, because it's so holy.  Limb protection is not so great, but at least you'll have your organs.
This used to be a Holy Servant's robe, now reduced to rags.
A crude suit made out of human skin, expertly torn off it's original owner in sheets and loosely tied on with wire.  The perfect disguise.
The Skin Bandits need a constant supply of fresh human skin to make new suits, as they tend to rot away quite quickly.
Some crazy dude at some point must have thought "I like hats, but I don't like helmets, but I also like having a sword-resistant head...".  Now we have iron hats.
A protective hood with steel plates on the sides.
A chain hood.

A long leather coat, offers a light protection from attacks.  Pretty hot to wear in the desert, but popular in the Swamps because of the constant rain.
Simple bindings to protect the bones of the fist.  Commonly worn by martial artists, those who shun the use of the sword.
A breathing mask that helps mitigate the negative health effects of fog.
A solid, heavy helmet with good protection of the face.  Often worn by bandits, as the high face guard also provides some anonymity.
A good all-round medium class armour, favoured by any warrior that has to travel across the wilds.

The only heavy armour that isn't affiliated with any particular faction, it's become standard with mercenaries and short-range wanderers.  
More of a medium-heavy class, it allows a little more versatility than other heavy armours.
Orange robes of the Holy Nation Priest caste, demanding respect from anyone lower than a High Paladin.
Wear this and you will be a real ninja!  (Warning: Not a substitute for real ninja training)
Keeps the wind and sand out of your face.  Also helps to hide your pasty face in the darkness.
Wear this and you will be a real ninja!  (Warning: Not a substitute for real ninja training)
A cover-up suit popular with theives and ninjas.  Helps cover your visibility and identity.
An expensive silk robe made by artisans of the Empire's capital.  Worn by nobles and the wealthy elite as a sign of status.

Tired of weak leather to protect your fat human legs?  Using the latest in the Hives research technology we have positioned metal stuff in no less than TWO key locations for optimal leg stab protection.  Queen-approved!

The standard armoured boots, found everywhere.  Commonly left out of an armour set, as drifters don't usually see much likelyhood in getting hit in the shins and prefer the reduced encumbrance of a pair of wooden sandals or even going barefoot altogether.
Nobody knows why it's called a Police Helmet, as the Samurai Police don't wear these.  Perhaps it's another Old Empire remnant.

Straw hats are common among everyone from peasant farmers to desert scouts and help shade the wearer from the intense heat of the sun.  Shading the eyes from glare can also provide a minor aid in combat.

Head plates were invented by an old forgotten clan that was obsessed with luck.  Before battle their prophets and shamans would predict where on their head the next fatal blow was due to land, then position the metal plate on their head accordingly.  Statistically, some would always turn out to be correct and those lucky ones, by virtue of surviving, would be the ones to return and spread word of the prophet's success, further reinforcing the belief.
Supposedly makes the wearer look a bit like a skeleton.
A creepy black duster coat worn by wierdos out of the Ashlands.  The sleveless version is favoured by martial artists.
A regular longcoat with the sleeves removed to provide better cooling for the wearer.  Commonly worn amongst the gangs of the swamps.
Some sort of crude helmet patched together out of scraps of plate, with added spikes for intimidation.  Guaranteed to be strapped to a bandit of some kind.
A simple eye protection for sandstorms, standard issue in the Traders Guild
A rough fabric favoured by the Holy Nation for its lack of comfort.
A rough fabric favoured by the Holy Nation for its lack of comfort.

Straw hats are common among everyone from peasant farmers to desert scouts and help shade the wearer from the intense heat of the sun.  Shading the eyes from glare can also provide a minor aid in combat.
A mask of the Swamp Ninjas of the south, it's purpose is unknown, likely it's either a tradition or an intimidation tactic.
A cover-up suit popular with theives and ninjas.  Helps cover your visibility and identity.
Quite a good head padding in a simple cloth.  It can be wrapped around the face to protect the eyes in a dust storm

The Tin Can is a super heavy-class helmet and makes for the best head protection around.  Heavy cuts and slashes against it will still make your head ring, but at least you will still have your face attached.  Unfortunately the limited field of view does hamper your combat awareness a fair bit.

The Traders Guild is proud of its claimed "rags to riches" origin story, and continues to use the leather wrap-around jacket as its unofficial uniform.  Although, being over 200 years old nobody can confirm the true origins of the Guild, and skeptics say the mundane clothing is just to make them seem more humble and honest, so you don't notice when they are ripping you off.
Once part of a uniform of the Old Empire, it seems to have hung around to this day.
Keeps the heat off your head and pads your brains.  It's often worn by slave traders in this style, and has started to become associated as being part of their uniform.
Good shirt for sneaking about, doing spy stuff.

Some mercenaries were interested in the capabilities of the Holy Nation's body armour, but didn't wan't the problems of appearing to be associated with the faction.  So they made their own copies without the religious faction logos painted all over it, and then blackened them in the forge.
A solid steel helmet with a protective visor.
A plated leather jacket with a good solid armour coverage. Commonly worn by the wealthier drifters and professional adventurer scouts.
Classical wooden sandals.  They take a bit of getting used to, but they're actually really good for running in sand.
A simple woollen hat, good for cold desert nights.

This arm is obviously made mostly out of salvaged parts from other skeleton arms, though they did make a functioning claw hand for it, quite an impressive feat of engineering in this age.  The limb cap is half a grog can with some padding inside.
They are good and cheap, but not very durable, and obviously your dexterity is going to suffer from having a claw for a hand.

The Hivers are extremely proud of the skeleton limbs that they supposedly manufacture themselves.  This "leg" obviously used to be a skeleton's arm, with the hand removed and half a grog can to act as a stump fitting.  They haven't added any foot, because Hivers don't understand the necessity for feet.
Still, they are the only modern day manufacturers of artificial limbs.  The natural go-to when you are low on funds and somethings eats off your leg.

An arm from an ancient logistics unit, it has exceptional strength.  
These units were used in the corporate factories and warehouses of the distant past.  Due to their inherent slowness they weren't adapted into combat units like their cousins, and remained behind in production roles before they were buried in the ash.

The KLR series was legendary for it's simple durability. Designed for the original service bots working alone in remote hostile environments, fancy features and luxuries were ditched in favor of simplicity.
Many were used on the frontlines of the war, so few can be found today.

Not the fastest legs around, but a heavy duty KLR leg like this one will keep on running when any normal person would be limping, so the cannibals won't be able to catch up to you and get any more of your limbs.

The leg of a rebel scout unit.
The design has been kept lightweight at the cost of durability, but is capable of impressive speed.

A common skeleton arm.  Though a few thousand years old, those that have survived in good condition can be more dexterous than human hands.

A well maintained piece of machinery, this arm has been carefully customised and upgraded by its previous owner.  The motor seems like a completely different unit and there's some kind of AI thralled into a feedback unit that provides adaptive stabilisation.

An old leg from one of the specialised assassination units from the war.  The rubberised footing has been renewed at some point in recent history, allowing for quiet movement instead of the usual CLANK sounds that most skeletons make when walking.

A heavily customised arm.  Somehow the components have almost no rust, and the mechanism is extremely smooth.
Backpack designed to fit Bulls
Backpack designed to fit Gars

This backpack is huge.  Don't even think about fighting with this on your back.  The thing weighs a ton just when its empty.  Do you seriously think you can fill it full of iron or something and be able to lift it?  Let alone carry it across the desert!?  Go get a smaller one.
A medium sized backpack, with a good weight distribution, so you can handle more weight.  It will hinder you a bit in combat though.
A cheap and useful backpack, commonly associated with peasants and scavengers.
A bag designed for shopkeepers.  Not for travelling around with.
A bag used by professional thieves and ninjas.  Well made and designed not to hinder your stealth while you fill it with other people's posessions.
A bag used by professional thieves and ninjas.  Well made and designed not to hinder your stealth while you fill it with other people's posessions.
A specialist backpack for traders.  Allows better stacking of large items within a smaller space, particularly trade goods.  Not designed to wear during a sword fight though.
A specialist backpack for traders.  Allows better stacking of large items within a smaller space, particularly trade goods
A wooden backpack with a built in sun shade. It's the height of luxury for the travelling trader.
A backpack that allows for better stacking of large items within a smaller space, particularly trade goods.
A high quality first aid kit, made up of bandages, disinfectant and painkillers.  Only worth the extra money if you have the skill to use it.
A splint kit can be used to rig up wounded bodyparts so that they can be used again.  The amount of hitpoints you can splint is limited by your medic skill and the quality of the kit.
A rare piece of ancient technology, anyone capable of researching it could unlock the most advanced technology of the modern age.

An ancient food ration that must be thousands of years old.  It's a sealed container that contains a dense cake that's surprisingly filling.  It's covered in printed writing and symbols that you don't recognise.
A valuable artifact from ancient times, detailing long-lost advanced technologies.
Skin taken from an animal, can be cured to make leather.
Hammered plates of metal used for crafting armour.
An authentic* repair kit of the very highest quality, designed and manufactured by the Advanced Skeleton Labs of the Western Hives.
Nobles pay a lot of money for this rare delicacy.  Many people die trying to steal them.
A fine rare spirit that rich people put on their shelves to impress their friends.
A book from the University of Machinists. Everything they learn is compiled into books like this one in an attempt to teach others and improve the world.
Horrible, dry dry bread.

A very strong alcohol common in the deserts.  Dehydrates you like nothing else, so considered a rare luxury, apart from when it gets imported into the greenlands, where water isn't an issue, then they drink it like madmen.
Trading material based on one of the old civilization's monetary systems, named after an old dictator.
A fancy ceramic bowl for rich people to eat their fancy food from, probably picking the food out with dainty little implements instead of just using their hands like normal people.
Raw sheets of chainmail used in armour crafting.  It takes an extremely long time to make, which jacks up the price.

The Chalice Of Fire, said to have been forged from the Sacred Flame by the 47th Holy Phoenix himself.



It just looks like a standard cup. But it IS very shiny.
Best you can do with nothing but cactuses
Trading material based on one of the old civilization's monetary systems.
Pretty basic food
Advanced alloy of steel and copper for specialised building work.
A valuable metal used in high-tech machinery.
Cotton is used to make fabrics and clothing.

Cat-Lon's dream was to rebuild civilisation and make up for past mistakes. His empire was vast and focused on study of the lost technologies. 
But a thousand years is a long time to live. You slowly accumulate fears and prejudices from your bad experiences.  You change, become angry.  Before you know it, you're a dictator.  Over time the population requires more and more force to keep them opressed.

Science and archaeology flourished in the empire until an explosion in the Grid caused a famine.

CPU of General Hat-12, who was chief of the empire police.  He launched a crackdown on the new cultists but his heavy handed approach only fueled their blame and confusion further. Things escalated faster.

CPU of General Jang, leader of the famous Hydraulic Knights. They fought on the frontlines to protect the empire from pirates and cannibals, their heroism legendary.  As time went on, the label of "pirate" became thrown around more and more gratuitously, and they found they were killing more of their own people than the real pirates were.
Rhinobot just wanted to help, but he had no moral processing, and so would help with anything, even the most diabolical evil.  He didn't see anything wrong with his child prisons.

He could never have forseen the events that happened, but he still blamed himself for the famine, and the subsequent downfall of the empire.
Supposedly a piece of brain from a Skeleton or maybe an Iron Spider.  Must be worth something to a collector.
A live crab egg, worth a little bit of money.
Various components used to make crossbows.
Whatever it was, it's pretty useless now.
An old child's toy, battered and worn beyond its prime.
Contrary to popular belief, Dried fish is not a third species of fish, it's just a Thinfish that's been dried and salted.
Good survival food
Possibly the food with the highest unpleasantness to nutrition ratio in the world. So dry. Probably a big contributor to desert suicide.
Complicated electricals and stuff, you wouldn't understand it.
Worthless
I feel let down
A rare artifact that can be used to unlock advanced building research.
General fabrics useful for general crafting purposes.
A wonderfully vibrant walking adornment, to enrich the ambience of the discerning dream home.

If you are reading this there is a good chance you just escaped from Rebirth and are half-dead.  This safehouse is for you to use to rest and recover, you should hopefully find here some food, tools to remove your shackles, beds, and some basic clothing.  Good Luck.

PS.  If you are just a passing adventurer, please don't loot this place, or we will hunt you down and skin you alive.  

PPS.  If you are a Holy Nation soldier, fuck you and fuck your dumb brain-washing religion, we will defy you to the end you poncy stuck-up slope-browed mouth-breathers. 

--Moll
The decapitated head of a Fogman Prince.  This trophy is worth a heavy bounty.
Disappointing but nutritious, squished into an efficient cube.
Uncooked meat from a poor quality source.  No good for eating.
Fuel is what keeps everything running. You need it for your generators.
Gear wheels, used in various machinery.
The vital core of any electricity-generating machine.  Weighs a ton.
Rice and vegetables, good food.
The Grand Fish, king of all the two known fish species in the world.
The severed claw from the gorillo of Mourn.
Skin taken from the rare Great White Gorillo.
It's not actually green or even a fruit, it's a vegetable.  Nobody knows why it's called this, but the habit continues.
An old machine from empires past.  Doesn't work.
A traditional canister of grog.  Quite weak as alcoholic drinks go, but that just means you can drink several times more of it.
A creepy Fishman egg, stolen from the Gurglers.
The decapitated head of a King Gurgler.  This trophy is worth a heavy bounty.
A metal saw. Could be used to remove slave shackles.
An ancient book of science that has been chewed up and half eaten by some kind of animal.  It's pretty useless now.

A narcotic product that can ruin your life by getting you arrested.  Effects include foolish giggling, increased sense of humor, and enjoyment of food. Narcotics are illegal in most towns and will get you busted if you are caught smuggling, however the potential profits are huge.  The traders guild won't touch them.  Despite all of this however, the drug remains popular, especially in borderland towns where the laws are less aggressively enforced.
Hemp is commonly used to make fabrics and clothing.

Special item. 

Reads: 'Absolver of the Infernal'

A seal given to you by the Holy Lord Phoenix, blessed be his name. Show it to paladins for aid.
A horn spike from the legendary Megaraptor, should fetch a good price.

headings: Uses of Iron Plates in Construction

factMedia.caption: Used for building machinery, or for further refinement into steel.
An old lantern. It looks pretty beaten up and barely functions. There are some worn out scratchings on it which look like the crude drawings of a child.
An important ingredient in crafting armour.  Good to stock up on as it can be hard to find.
The pearl of a Leviathan! What a trophy, it's worth a fortune.
Meat in some bread. It's great.
Some kind of organ or something that was inside the Megacrab.  Whatever it is, it's probably worth a bit of money

A membership pack given to new members of the Traders Guild.








It contains countless pages of rambling legal mumbo jumbo, each individually stamped with the seal of the Traders Guild. You could probably just chuck it away, free up some storage space... but you just know there's a tiny chance that as soon as you do that, somebody will ask you for it. 







Noble world problems.
A device that can create rotation when charged with electrical current.
It contains the half chewed stone of a greenfruit. It has Tengu's saliva on it, maybe that's worth something, right?... Right?

Special item. 

A sealed note given to you from Moll to give to Flotsam Ninja patrols. Whoever you give it to will become a useful temporary ally against the Holy Nation.
Looks like it has been damaged from overheating.  It's a miracle this skeleton was still alive.
An old map of some other, probably fictional, continent.  Pretty useless, but maybe you can get some money for it.
A fancy decorative thing used by extremely rich people to clutter up their houses.
A fancy decorative thing used by extremely rich people to clutter up their houses.
A fancy decorative thing used by extremely rich people to clutter up their houses.
A fancy decorative thing used by extremely rich people to clutter up their houses.
Some kind of ancient tech, possibly a Skeleton's heart or liver or something.
Raw metal is used to make Steel Bars
Uncooked meat from some dead animal.  Probably.
Raw stone is used to make building materials.
A plain staple food
A nutritious weed that grows in wet environments like swamps.
No longer edible, such a waste.
A strong alcohol made in the swamps, but popular among samurai and frequently imported by the Empire towns.
Something basic for the floor of your building.
Some kind of electrical glass eye like the ones the Skeletons have.
Also known to engineers as "Hydraulics", they are what makes a Skeleton's arms and legs move.
The equivalent of a first aid kit for Skeletons, contains tools and common robotic components

Essential for any traveller.  Carry one of these around with you and you can build yourself a camp bed anywhere you need it.  Finding some time to rest up and heal in the wilds can save your life.  (Use BUILD mode to place a camp bed)
A small sculpture of the Holy Nations Emperor.

A splint kit can be used to rig up wounded bodyparts so that they can be used again.  Useful if you have a leg injury and don't want to limp all the way back to town, you can splint up your leg and regain a little functionality.

They also have the bonus that any splinted damage counts against limb amputation in combat.

The amount of hitpoints you can splint is limited by your medic skill and the quality of the kit.
A flexible metal used in crossbows and machinery.
A first aid kit, made up of bandages, disinfectant and painkillers.  The quality will limit you if it is lower than your skills.
Strawflour can be used to make bread.  Horrible, dry dry bread.

images: The Little Boy That Got Dismembered By Skeletons
factMedia.caption:
"The number one, best selling children's book of today! 

Little Timmy liked climbing trees and playing hide and seek with his friends, but he always skipped on his prayers. Then Timmy met his first Skeleton.."
Found in the larger lakes of the swamps and wetlands, the blandly-named Thinfish. So called because it's thinner than the other type of fish.

A pack of tools.  Can be used to cut through locks and to remove slave shackles.  They tend to break pretty often and are usually discarded after use. 

Cutting through locks is a lot slower and noisier than picking.  They are commonly used by more honest folk such as treasure hunters breaking into old vaults.
Wheatstraw is one of the few crops that can be grown in arid environments.  Its a sturdy crop, and can be used to make horrible flat bread or rum that makes you go blind.
This looks like it could be a valuable find, it details the location of an Old Empire military cache.  It might have some valuable equipment

It's a map pointing to a certain location in the Ashlands.  It's covered in gibberish writing and pictograms.
Though the Bugmaster was obviously insane, he seemed to have lived long and knew a lot of the world's secrets. 
You can piece together enough scraps of information to understand that the Bugmaster was training himself in preparation to go here and kill someone.  It seems to have been his obsession.

Whoever is there waiting in the Ashlands, it must be someone insanely dangerous.
This is an ancient document by an engineer of the old empire, it details potential sites where you could find Engineering Research.
A map of the Holy Nation homelands around Okran's Valley.  Some of the farms and mines can be good for trading.
An actual map of a known location in the fabled Ashlands.  This could be worth a fortune.
A no-man's land between the three great nations, conflict prevents civilised settlement.
An easy place to get lost, well worth buying a map for.

images: Map of the United Cities (Central Territories)
factMedia.caption: A map of all the main towns of the United Cities around the Great Desert area
The mysterious homelands of the Western Hive.  Humans don't tend to venture there.
For those desperate enough to face a fate worse than death, a promise of isolated safety and a future without slavery.
World's End is an outland stronghold of the Machinist's University.  Tech Hunters use it as the main homebase when exploring the north.

A treasure map for some ancient ruin.  Likely full of treasure or lost technology or horrible death.  The map is insanely old and hard to understand, but from what you can gather it appears to be something science or technology related.  It could have Ancient Science Books, or possibly even AI Cores.

This seems to be a top secret military document from the Holy Nation.  It contains orders for a secret special unit of sentinels that guard some kind of secret that they refer to as "Narko's Trap".
The location of the base is included with a map.
A hand-drawn map marking a location of interest to the Tech Hunters.  It's likely to be an oldworld information source that could reveal the locations of Labs.
A map from a Tech Hunter scout, detailing a possible location to find Ancient Science Books.
